sources.title: 34 CFR Part 34 — Administrative Wage Garnishment (federal student loan default; 34 CFR 34.19's 15%-of-disposable-pay / 30x-minimum-wage-floor rule)
sources.verifiedBy: Cross-source confirmed via search synthesis, not an independently rendered direct fetch this pass.

$scopeNote: Covers the three garnishment types a per-paycheck engine can actually compute from a single check in isolation: ordinary (consumer/creditor) judgment garnishment, child support/alimony income-withholding orders, and federal student loan default administrative wage garnishment. A federal TAX LEVY is deliberately NOT modelled here — its exempt amount depends on IRS Publication 1494's own table (filing status, number of dependents, standard deduction, updated annually) rather than a fixed CCPA fraction, a genuinely different calculation this file doesn't attempt. See src/garnishment.ts's own module comment for how these interact when more than one order is in effect on the same paycheck.

ordinaryGarnishment.$note: 15 U.S.C. 1673(a) / 29 CFR 870.10: the lesser of 25% of disposable earnings, or the amount by which disposable earnings exceed 30x the federal minimum hourly wage, for a WEEKLY pay period. 29 CFR 870.10 separately names 60/65/130 as the equivalent multipliers for biweekly/semimonthly/monthly; every other pay frequency this engine supports (daily, quarterly, semiannual, annual) is this project's own consistent extension of the same ratio (30 * 52 / periodsPerYear), not independently sourced for those frequencies.

supportOrder.$note: 15 U.S.C. 1673(b): up to 50% of disposable earnings if the employee is supporting a spouse or child not covered by the order, up to 60% if not; either figure rises by 5 points (to 55%/65%) if any part of the support obligation is more than 12 weeks in arrears. This engine does NOT assume a default for supportingOtherFamily — the caller states it, same discipline as everywhere else this engine refuses to guess an eligibility fact.

studentLoanDefault.$note: 34 CFR 34.19: lesser of 15% of disposable pay or the same 30x-minimum-wage floor ordinary garnishment uses. Combined with any OTHER garnishment already in effect on the same paycheck, total withholding still may not exceed the 25% CCPA aggregate ceiling — enforced in src/garnishment.ts by aggregate-room accounting shared across all non-support orders, not by a separate field here.
